instruction: Check which files a recursive delete would remove before deleting anything.
context: Run the selecting expression with -print first and only swap in -delete once the list is right. find -delete gives no confirmation and no undo, so the preview is the only safety step available.

instruction: Delete a directory tree but get one confirmation prompt first.
context: rm: capital -I prompts once before removing more than three files or recursing, which is usable where lowercase -i prompts per file and trains you to hold down y. -I is GNU-only.

instruction: Remove a build directory by an explicit relative path.
context: Anchor recursive deletes with ./ and a literal name. An unquoted variable that expands to empty turns rm -rf $DIR/ into rm -rf /, which is why GNU rm refuses / unless --no-preserve-root is passed.

instruction: Delete a file whose name begins with a dash.
context: The -- separator ends option parsing, so everything after it is treated as a filename however it is spelled. Without it, a file literally named -rf is read as flags. ./-rf also works.

instruction: Set aside files I think are unused without permanently deleting them.
context: Moving to a holding directory is reversible where rm is not, and it costs nothing on the same filesystem because only the directory entry changes. Delete the holding area once the change is verified.

instruction: Move a file without silently overwriting an existing one.
context: mv: -n refuses to overwrite an existing destination and exits quietly, while -i asks. Bare mv overwrites without a word, which is how files disappear during a reorganization.

instruction: Overwrite a file but keep a copy of what was there.
context: mv and cp accept --backup, where numbered keeps app.conf.~1~, app.conf.~2~ and so on. --backup=simple keeps only the most recent, suffixed with a tilde.

instruction: Copy files into a directory only where they do not already exist.
context: cp: -n skips existing destinations. When both -n and -i are given the last one on the command line wins, so mixing them produces whichever behaviour was written second.

instruction: Write a disk image to a removable device and watch the progress.
response: dd if=image.iso of=/dev/sdx bs=4M status=progress conv=fsync
context: dd: verify of= names the intended device with lsblk immediately beforehand, because dd overwrites without confirmation and a wrong letter destroys the system disk. status=progress reports throughput and conv=fsync flushes before exit.

instruction: Confirm which device node is the USB stick before writing to it.
context: Device letters are assignment-ordered and change between boots, so /dev/sdb is not stable. Match on SIZE and MODEL rather than the name, and confirm the target has no system mountpoint.

instruction: Reclaim space from a huge log file that a running service still has open.
context: Truncating in place keeps the inode, so the writing process keeps appending to the same descriptor. Deleting the file instead frees nothing until the service restarts, because the open handle holds the blocks.

instruction: Fix permissions on regular files only, leaving directories alone.
context: Selecting with find -type f keeps a recursive chmod from clearing the execute bit directories need to be traversable. chmod -R 644 on a tree makes every directory unenterable, including the one you are standing in.

instruction: Change ownership of symlinks without touching what they point at.
context: chown: -h acts on the symlink itself. Without it, a recursive chown follows links out of the tree and can silently reassign ownership of system files the links happen to reference.

instruction: See what a mirroring sync would delete on the destination.
context: rsync --delete removes destination files missing from the source, and a mistyped source path makes that the whole destination. -n previews and --stats summarizes the counts before committing.

instruction: List untracked files a clean would remove, including ignored ones.
context: git clean: -n previews, -d includes untracked directories, and -x also removes ignored files such as .env and local caches. Those are exactly the files with no copy in history, so -x deserves the preview most.

instruction: Record the current state before doing something destructive to the branch.
context: Committed work is recoverable through the reflog, but uncommitted changes are not, and reset --hard discards them outright. Stashing with -u captures tracked and untracked work into a recoverable object first.

instruction: Check which processes a pattern-based kill would hit.
context: Run pgrep with the exact flags first, because pkill uses the same matching and prints nothing about what it signalled. A loose pattern with -f can match a text editor holding the filename in its command line.

instruction: Avoid running a command at all when the input list is empty.
context: xargs: without -r, GNU xargs runs the command once with no arguments when input is empty, which turns an empty match list into a bare command run in the current directory. BSD xargs does this by default and has no -r.

instruction: Preview the exact commands a find and xargs pipeline would run.
context: Inserting echo before the real command prints each assembled invocation without running it, showing how arguments are batched and quoted. Remove echo once the printed commands are correct.

instruction: Edit files in place while keeping the originals.
context: sed: attaching a suffix to -i writes the original to config.toml.bak before editing. A bare -i on GNU sed edits with no backup at all, and a bad regex is then unrecoverable.

instruction: Check what a substitution will change before writing it to the file.
context: sed: -n suppresses automatic printing and the p flag on the s command prints only the lines that actually matched. This shows the edit set without -i touching anything.

instruction: Stop shell redirection from silently overwriting existing files.
context: With noclobber set, > fails on an existing file and >| overrides it for that one command. This catches the transposition of > for >> before it empties a log.

instruction: Add a line to a root-owned config without truncating it.
context: tee -a appends where bare tee truncates first. sudo tee is also the way to write a privileged file from a pipeline, because sudo cmd > file applies the redirection as the unprivileged user.

instruction: Protect a critical config file from accidental modification or deletion.
context: chattr: the immutable attribute blocks writes, renames, and deletion even for root until it is cleared with -i. lsattr shows current attributes; this is ext4 and xfs specific.

instruction: Download an install script to read it before executing it.
context: Saving to a file separates fetch from execute, so the contents can be reviewed. Piping curl straight into a shell gives the server a different response for the piped request than for a browser fetch.

instruction: Verify a downloaded file against its published checksum file.
context: sha256sum: -c reads a checksum file and verifies each listed path, reporting OK or FAILED per entry and exiting non-zero on any mismatch. --ignore-missing skips entries not present locally.

instruction: Verify a detached signature on a release artifact.
context: gpg --verify takes the signature first and the signed file second. A good signature from an untrusted key still reports success with a warning, so the key fingerprint must be checked separately.

instruction: Enter a token interactively so it never reaches the shell history file.
context: read: -s suppresses echo and -r stops backslash interpretation. Typing a secret as a command argument records it in history and exposes it in ps output for the lifetime of the process.

instruction: Restrict a credentials file so only its owner can read it.
context: Mode 0600 is owner read and write with nothing for group or other. ssh refuses to use private keys with looser modes, and the same standard suits any file holding credentials.

instruction: Check a sudoers edit for syntax errors before it takes effect.
context: visudo -c parses every sudoers file and reports errors without installing anything. A syntax error written directly into /etc/sudoers locks out sudo entirely, and there is no second chance to fix it.

instruction: See which symlinks enabling a service would create, without creating them.
context: systemctl: --dry-run prints the link and unlink operations that would be performed and changes nothing. It applies to enable, disable, mask, and preset.

instruction: Find out what removing a package would also uninstall.
context: apt-get: -s simulates and prints the full action list without root or any change to the system. Removing a widely depended-on library often cascades into dozens of packages, which the simulation reveals first.

instruction: Check how much space docker is using before pruning anything.
context: docker system df: -v breaks the totals down per image, container, and volume so the reclaimable figure is attributable. docker system prune -a --volumes deletes named volumes, which usually hold the only copy of local data.

instruction: Validate a manifest against the cluster without applying it.
context: kubectl: --dry-run=server sends the request through admission controllers and validation but does not persist it, catching schema and webhook errors. --dry-run=client only checks locally and misses those.

instruction: Confirm which cluster I am pointed at before running a destructive command.
context: The active context persists across shells and sessions, so the last cluster selected is still selected tomorrow. Checking it is the step that separates deleting a staging deployment from deleting the production one.

instruction: Make sure the changes I reviewed are exactly the ones that get applied.
context: Saving the plan to a file and applying that file guarantees the applied change set is the reviewed one. A bare apply re-plans at execution time, so drift between review and apply is silently included.

instruction: Run a migration script so any error rolls the whole thing back.
context: psql: -1 wraps the file in a single transaction and ON_ERROR_STOP=1 aborts on the first error. Without both, psql continues past failures and commits each statement, leaving a half-applied migration.

instruction: Remove a stale host key after a server was rebuilt.
context: ssh-keygen -R deletes that host's entry from known_hosts, which is the correct fix after a legitimate rebuild. Disabling StrictHostKeyChecking instead removes the warning for every host permanently.

instruction: Edit a file in place on macOS while keeping the original.
context: BSD sed requires -i to take a separate suffix argument, so -i '.bak' keeps a backup and -i '' keeps none. The GNU attached form -i.bak is read by BSD sed as the script, which corrupts the command.

instruction: Handle an empty input list safely on macOS.
context: BSD xargs already skips execution on empty input and rejects the GNU -r flag outright. Scripts meant to run on both platforms therefore cannot simply pass -r unconditionally.

instruction: Identify the right device before writing an image on macOS.
context: macOS has no lsblk; diskutil list shows each disk with its size and partitions. Use the raw node /dev/rdiskN for dd because it is markedly faster than the buffered /dev/diskN.
